The drug is linked to Dual serine/threonine and tyrosine protein kinase, which in turn is targeted by 6-Acetonyldihydrochelerythrine and Npc115753, both of which also target H9. Additionally, Epi-Fibrauretinoside A is associated with Valacyclovir hydrolase, which is targeted by 5''-(2''''-Hydroxyphenyl)-Methyluvarinol, which also targets H9. These pathways suggest that Epi-Fibrauretinoside A may exert its effects through a series of molecular intermediates that ultimately engage H9. The integration of these targets highlights a potential mechanism by which the drug influences H9, though the exact nature of the interaction remains to be fully elucidated.
